FOREWORD 



This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 4 March 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Automotive Vehicle Testing and Performance of Evaluation Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 



IS 12695 :. J,989 



Indian Standard 



AUTOMOTIVE VEHICLES — 

THREE WHEELED VEHICLES — 

DETERMINATION OF CENTRE OF GRAVITY 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the method of 
determining the position of centre of gravity of 
three wheeled vehicles, namely, autorickshaws 
and three wheeled passenger cars.

3 TERMS AND DEFINITIONS 

3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the follow- 
ing terms and definitions shall apply. 



POSITION OF CG 




3.1 Position of Centre of Gravity 

The position of centre of gravity on a hori- 
zontal plane shall be defined on the longitudinal 
and the transverse axes as follows ( sec Fig. 1 ). 

3.1.1 Position of centre of gravity along the 
longitudinal axis is defined as the least distance 
of centre of gravity in millimetres from a trans- 
verse vertical plane passing through the centre 
line of the front wheel of the vehicle. This is 
represented by X ia Fig. 1. 

3.1.2 Position of centre of gravity along trans- 
verse axis of the vehicle is defined as the least 
distance of centre of gravity in millimetres from 
a longitudinal median plane passing through 
the longitudinal centre line of the vehicle. This 
position of centre of gravity may be on left or 
right hand side of the longitudinal vertical plane 
with reference to driver when seated in the 
driving seat. This is represented by. Y in Fig. I. 

3.2 Height of Centre of Gravity 

It is the height of centre of gravity in millimetres 
from the supporting surface when the vehicle is 
placed on a plain level horizontal surface. This 
is represented by Z in Fig. I.

4.1 The following abbreviations have been used 
while deriving the formulae for determining the 
position and height of centre of gravity for a 
three wheeled ( CG ) vehicle: 

W^ ~ mass on front wheel (kg); 

PF2 = mass on rear right wheel ( kg ); 

PF3 ~ mass on rear left wheel ( kg ); 

W ^ vehicle kerb mass ( kg )--=W^+W2+lV^; 

Wi = mass on rear axle ( kg ) when the 
vehicle has been lifted through certain 
height Yx from the front; 

L ^--^ average wheel base ( mm ); 

Ki ^ extent of lift ( mm ), that is, difference 
in heights of centres of front and rear 
wheels from ground level when the 
vehicle has been lifted from the front; 



X ~ distance of CG from the centre of the 
front wheel along the longitudinal axis 
of the vehicle in mm ( see 3.2 ); 

Y =- distance of CG on transverse axis 
towards left side or the right hand 
side of longitudinal axis of the vehicle 
in mm; 
Z == height of centre of gravity on vertical 
axis ( mm ) from the ground level ( see 
Fig. 1 ); 
a " rear wheel track ( mm ); and 
r — rolling radius of wheels ( mm ).

may be experimentally determined by weighing 
the rear axle load when the rear wheels are rest-

single wheel being lifted through certain height 
Yi from ground level ( see Fig. 4).

5 PREPARATION OF THE VEHICLE 

5.1 The vehicle shall conform in all its parts and 
components to the design and/or production 
series. 



REAR 




FRONT 



Fig. 4 Height of Centre of Gravity on Vertical Axis 

3 



IS 12695 : 1989 



5.2 The tyres fitted on the vehicle shall not have 
done more than 10 percent of its life and shall be 
inflated to the pressure recommended by the 
vehicle manufacturer. 

5.3 The vehicle loading shall be as per the vehicle 
kerb weight as defined in IS 11422 : 1986. 

5.4 All axle suspensions of the vehicle shall be 
locked by some means so that its springs do not 
get deflected during the tests. 

6 TEST PROCEDURE 

6.1 After the preparation of the vehicle, the 
following procedure shall be followed for deter- 
mining the position and height of CG of the 
three wheeled vehicle. 

6.2 The front wheel, rear right wheel and rear 
left wheel loading of the test vehicle shall be 
measured separately on a weigh-bridge. These 
loading values shall be denoted by fFi, W2 and 
^3, respectively. 

6.3 The kerb mass of the test vehicle shall be 
measured and denoted by W, 

6.4 The wheel base shall be measured on both 
the sides and the average wheel base shall be 
found out. This shall be denoted by L. 

6.5 The rear wheel track of vehicle shall be 
measured and denoted by a. 

6.6 The static rolling radius of the wheel of the 
test vehicle shall be measured and denoted by r. 



6.7 The test vehicle shall be positioned on the 
platform of weigh-bridge in such a way that the 
rear wheels will be on the weighing platform 
whereas the front wheel will remain outside on 
the same level. 

6.8 The parking brake of the vehicle shall be 
applied and the engine shall be switched off. 

6.9 The front wheel of the vehicle which is out- 
side the weighing platform shall be lifted by 
means of an anchoring hook and a crane so that 
the angle through which the vehicle is tilted does 
not exceed 10 to 12'' ( approx ). 

6.10 Note the rear axle loading value in the lifted 
position. Denote this by W^, 

6.11 The position and height of centre of gravity 
of the test vehicle can be worked out from the 
following formulae: 

a) Position of CG along longitudinal axis 

from the centre of the front wheel ( X )

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is joverned by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 a,nd the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.
